QUOTE: Binary detection runs before parsing. Non-text files are skipped, but there is no size limit, so a large generated `.c` is still read.
VERDICT: MISS
WHY: The answer describes binary detection as a content check and puts extension filtering in doxygen, but it never says the resolved scope is only part of the answer. It also never names the parse-built front end or the binary filter that drops files whose extension lies about them.
